After a live workspace artifact update, six concurrent gateway calls produced exactly one new bridge ingest log entry, showing that concurrent callers shared one bridge import/index-refresh pass for the same resolved config identity. The atomic source-page rewrite pressure probe did not break imports or final status, and the adjacent unknown-method probe returned a structured gateway error without destabilizing the gateway.
- **What was not tested:** The live race probe did not emit a directly observable `path-mismatch`/`FsSafeError` log signal, so this update does not claim a naturally observed path-mismatch recovery event; it proves the gateway stayed healthy under source-page atomic rewrite pressure and the code-level retry remains bounded to that transient error. I did not rerun the reporter-scale ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload, external channel delivery, or third-party provider/API proof on this head.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 [P1] exact-head real behavior proof for bridge gateway methods and retry/coalescing behavior:** Addressed for the real gateway surface on exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422`. `wiki.status`, `wiki.importInsights`, `wiki.palace`, and `wiki.bridge.import` all succeeded against bridge mode with a real public memory artifact; the concurrent six-call probe produced exactly one new ingest entry. Remaining gap: the live rewrite-pressure probe did not naturally surface a `path-mismatch` log/error signal, so that part is disclosed instead of overstated.
- **RF-002 [P1] live/local bridge proof gap:** Addressed with an isolated loopback OpenClaw gateway, memory-core + memory-wiki loaded, `vaultMode=bridge`, `bridge.readMemoryArtifacts=true`, and `bridgePublicArtifactCount=1` from an actual workspace `MEMORY.md` artifact.
- **RF-003 [P1] session-state / coalescing identity risk:** Addressed by the implementation and runtime probe. The coalescing key includes vault path/mode, bridge/ingest/render/search/context/obsidian config, and agent default/list workspace identity; the runtime concurrent batch updated the live artifact once and produced a single ingest delta across six gateway calls.
- **RF-004 [P1] stale gateway-load / reporter-scale proof:** Partially addressed and partially disclosed. This update supplies exact-head local gateway proof and fresh focused Vitest results after the rebase/conflict resolution; it does not claim the reporter's ~1,900-file WSL2/RSS-pressure workload was rerun.
- **RF-005 [maintainer decision] merge-risk / canonical retry acceptance:** Still requires maintainer judgment. This rebase keeps current main's shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing; maintainers should make the final broad-vs-narrow canonical merge decision.
- **RF-006 [signal] fresh proof / re-review:** This update replaces stale pre-rebase proof with current-head runtime gateway evidence and records it through the daily-fix verification marker. Remaining proof gaps are explicitly listed in `What was not tested` rather than hidden behind local tests.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- ClawSweeper previously flagged overlap with #94443 on transient `path-mismatch` retry behavior.
- This conflict resolution uses the current main shared `writeGuardedVaultPage` retry behavior for the guarded write boundary and keeps this PR focused on imported-source stat/read retry plus bridge import/index-refresh coalescing.
- This avoids restoring a divergent direct write retry path, but it does not override the remaining maintainer choice about broad-vs-narrow canonical merge direction.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts`, `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** coalesced concurrent imported-source sync for identical bridge config, separate coalescing identity when workspace inputs differ, transient imported-source `path-mismatch` retry, preserved human Notes, and preserved symlink/path-alias + directory-collision refusal.
- **Command:**

```bash
cd "/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-91828"
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-page-shared.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.test.ts \
  extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts
```

- **Result:** `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 22 passed (22)` in `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-91828-evidence/focused-vitest-after-sync.log`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** these tests and the runtime gateway proof exercise the memory-wiki import/sync owner boundary that calls `syncImportedSourcesIfNeeded`; they avoid coupling the guardrail to unrelated channel delivery, provider routing, or UI behavior.

## Origin / follow-up

Existing PR tied to #91154. This update rebases the existing PR, resolves the source-page conflict, and revalidates exact head `263d3858aea0106b5097db1f354b3494046da422` through the local gateway surface. After proof, daily-fix rechecked drift against `origin/main` ref `48e8965b1060d61beda1a52d572373a409317498`; there were no overlapping changed files and no sync-main requirement.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`, `extensions: memory-wiki`.
- **Risk explanation:** Behavior change is limited to memory-wiki import/sync coalescing and imported source-page retry; concurrent callers now share one underlying bridge import/index-refresh pass for the same resolved config identity.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is confined to `extensions/memory-wiki`, coalescing identity includes the bridge artifact-discovery inputs that can change imported source results, and the runtime gateway proof shows repeated/concurrent bridge calls produce one consistent bridge source page and no warnings. Existing symlink/path-alias safety remains outside the retry path.
- **Remaining maintainer decision:** Accept whether this focused imported-source retry/coalescing patch is the desired canonical merge path alongside the broader guarded write behavior already present on main.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Concurrent bridge imported-source syncs for the same vault/config each performed independent artifact-discovery + import/index-refresh passes, and imported source-page stat/read/write treated transient fs-safe `path-mismatch` races as fatal.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix coalesces at the import/sync source boundary, where bridge artifact discovery and index refresh are owned, and adds bounded retry only for the identified transient filesystem condition rather than masking downstream failures or weakening path safety.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high: the exact-head gateway proof covers the bridge surface and concurrent coalescing behavior; confidence is bounded by the disclosed missing natural `path-mismatch` signal and missing reporter-scale WSL2/RSS workload.
- **Patch quality notes:** No skipped-test or lint suppression claims; no broad refactor. The catch/default paths are narrow guard behavior: `path-mismatch` is rethrown into the bounded retry loop, `not-found`/race reads are treated as no preservable existing notes, and the actual write remains guarded by `writeGuardedVaultPage`, so symlink/path-alias safety is not masked.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** Source-of-truth boundary: `source-sync.ts` and `bridge.ts` own bridge artifact discovery, import, and index refresh; `source-page-shared.ts` owns imported source-page retry; `writeGuardedVaultPage` remains the canonical guarded vault write contract from main. Gateway methods are callers of this owner path, not new contract owners.

target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: fresh clone of `pull/99954/head` (`82bc62ed46`) inside a stock `node:22-bookworm` container: `git fetch --depth 1 origin pull/99954/head && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: plain Docker container (crabbox delegated providers unavailable on this host: `blacksmith` and `sbx` binaries not installed, no AWS credentials — stated per proof policy rather than skipped silently)
- Result: **34/34 tests passed, 6/6 files** on the fresh clone

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.

target.title: Add Teams delegated auth for plugin tools
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Plugin tools could not safely request a per-user Microsoft Teams delegated token from the current Teams conversation.
- Why it matters: Teams/Graph OBO-style integrations need user-delegated context without leaking channel tokens into prompts, transcripts, or broad plugin surfaces.
- What changed: Added generic plugin delegated-auth policy, runtime propagation, Teams Bot Framework SSO handling, Codex tool forwarding, docs, and a production-shaped example plugin/downstream API.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Delegated auth is implemented for Microsoft Teams only; non-Teams channels are not broadened by this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature

- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: End-to-end Teams delegated-auth consent for an OpenClaw plugin tool, including missing-consent handling, Bot Framework sign-in fallback, six-digit code completion, and retrying the tool with delegated auth available.
- Real environment tested: Local macOS OpenClaw dev checkout, `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`, Microsoft Teams dev app, Bot Framework OAuth connection, devtunnel on port 3978, local downstream OBO API, and the example `msteams-graph-profile` plugin.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. Started the local downstream OBO API.
  2. Started the OpenClaw dev gateway with the Teams channel and `msteams-graph-profile` plugin configured.
  3. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` to the OpenClaw Teams dev app.
  4. Opened the Bot Framework sign-in link rendered in Teams.
  5. Completed Microsoft sign-in/consent and sent the six-digit fallback code back to the Teams chat.
  6. Sent `hi, run teams whoami` again.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): Teams chat screenshot plus copied live output:
  ![Teams delegated auth proof](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/MSNexploder/b74c1786560f164ff726f52605204e33/raw/teams-delegated-auth-proof.png)
  ```text
  msteams_whoami ran again. Result:
  Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent

  Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.

  Success again:
  Stefan Stüben <redacted email>
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The initial tool run requested consent, the six-digit fallback completed the Teams delegated-auth flow, and the retried `msteams_whoami` call returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email through the downstream OBO API.
- What was not tested: Non-Teams channels, production-hosted downstream API deployment, broad tenant rollout beyond the dev tenant, and every Teams client rendering variant. The observed Teams client rendered the Bot Framework OAuth flow as a sign-in link fallback; the fallback and six-digit completion path were tested.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before consent, `msteams_whoami` returned `Microsoft Teams delegated auth unavailable: missing_consent`.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: N/A. This PR adds a new capability.
- Missing detection / guardrail: N/A.
- Contributing context (if known): Existing plugin tool execution had no channel-delegated auth context or Teams SSO consent bridge.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A for a new feature, but the smallest reliable guardrails added/used are:

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/plugins/tools.optional.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler.sso.test.ts`, `extensions/msteams/src/monitor-handler/message-handler.delegated-auth.test.ts`, `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`, `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.delegated-auth-context.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts`.
- Scenario the test should lock in: Delegated auth is available only when policy allows it, propagates through agent/tool execution paths, survives cached plugin descriptors, handles Teams missing-consent/sign-in flows, and does not swallow ordinary six-digit messages without a pending auth challenge.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: These tests cover the generic plugin policy seam, the Teams SSO edge cases, and the runtime paths that carry hidden delegated-auth context without requiring live Microsoft infrastructure in CI.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A before this PR.
- If no new test is added, why not: New tests were added/updated.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugin authors can opt into delegated auth with `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess`.
- Microsoft Teams plugin tools can request a Teams delegated token for the current user/conversation when explicitly allowlisted by config.
- Teams users may see a Bot Framework sign-in link/fallback when a delegated-auth tool needs consent.
- Added docs for Teams delegated-auth setup and plugin author usage.
- Added `examples/plugins/msteams-graph-profile` and `examples/msteams-obo-downstream-api`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Teams message -> agent -> plugin tool -> no delegated Teams user token -> downstream OBO unavailable

After:
Teams message -> Teams SSO provider -> gated plugin ctx.auth -> plugin tool -> downstream API OBO -> Microsoft Graph profile
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes`)
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Delegated Teams tokens are sensitive. This PR keeps access opt-in and policy-gated by plugin/tool allowlists plus provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type checks. Tokens are passed as hidden runtime context to plugin execution, not prompt text or transcript content. The example keeps Microsoft Graph access server-side in a downstream API so client secrets and Graph permissions stay behind an API boundary.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node/pnpm local dev checkout
- Model/provider: OpenAI dev agent profile
- Integration/channel (if any): Microsoft Teams dev app via devtunnel, Bot Framework OAuth connection
- Relevant config (redacted): Teams channel enabled, delegated-auth plugin entry enabled, local downstream OBO API configured with redacted client secret and app ids.

### Steps

1. Start devtunnel for the Teams bot endpoint on port 3978.
2. Start the local downstream OBO API.
3. Start `pnpm openclaw --dev gateway`.
4. Send `hi, run teams whoami` in Teams.
5. Complete the Bot Framework sign-in link and send the six-digit fallback code.
6. Retry `hi, run teams whoami`.

### Expected

- First run requests consent.
- Six-digit fallback completes delegated auth.
- Retried tool returns the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

### Actual

- First run returned `missing_consent`.
- Teams received the Bot Framework sign-in link.
- Six-digit fallback completed with `Microsoft Teams delegated auth is connected. Retry the tool now.`
- Retried `msteams_whoami` returned the signed-in Teams user profile/email.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: Teams missing-consent flow, Bot Framework sign-in link fallback, six-digit code completion, retrying `msteams_whoami`, and downstream OBO profile lookup.
- Edge cases checked: Six-digit messages are handled only while a pending sign-in challenge exists; delegated auth is rejected when missing/unconfigured/unavailable; Teams user-id fallback paths are covered by tests.
- What you did **not** verify: Non-Teams channels, production tenant rollout, hosted downstream API deployment, and every Teams client native OAuth-card rendering variant.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`Yes`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: Existing configs continue to work. To use delegated auth, explicitly configure `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess` and the Teams Bot Framework OAuth connection described in the docs.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A plugin could receive a user token unexpectedly.
  - Mitigation: Delegated auth is opt-in, allowlist-gated, and claim-validated before tool execution.
- Risk: Teams clients may render OAuth consent as a sign-in link instead of a native card.
  - Mitigation: The Teams implementation supports sign-in-link fallback and six-digit completion.
- Risk: Downstream API consent is separate from Teams bot consent.
  - Mitigation: Docs and examples use separate app registrations and document admin pre-consent for the downstream API.

## Rationale And Design Decisions

### Keep core generic

Delegated auth is modeled as a generic plugin capability instead of a Teams-specific special case in core. Core owns policy parsing, tool gating, token claim validation, and runtime propagation; the Teams plugin owns Bot Framework SSO behavior and token acquisition.

### Make delegated auth explicit and policy-gated

Plugin delegated auth is opt-in through `plugins.entries.<pluginId>.auth.delegatedAccess.enabled`, with optional provider, audience, scope, user, tenant, chat, and chat-type restrictions.

### Keep optional tools least-privilege

Optional plugin factories receive `ctx.auth` only when the plugin itself, `group:plugins`, `*`, or a concrete optional tool name is allowlisted. The resolver also handles implicit optional registrations where `names: []` and `declaredNames` carry the actual tool contract.

### Resolve auth per execution for cached descriptors

Cached plugin tool descriptors keep descriptor creation fast, but delegated auth is resolved when the cached tool executes, so a previous message’s auth context is never cached into a future run.

### Propagate auth through run plumbing, not prompts

The Teams delegated auth context is passed through hidden runtime/run parameters and plugin tool context, including queued replies, follow-up runs, embedded runner attempts, OpenClaw tools, and Codex app-server tool calls.

### Teams owns Bot Framework SSO details

The Teams plugin owns Bot Framework token exchange, verify-state, sign-in resource creation, sign-in-link fallback, six-digit code fallback, and Teams user-id fallback handling.

### Keep Graph access server-side in the example

The example plugin calls a local downstream API. The downstream API performs Microsoft Graph OBO using its own app registration and delegated permission grant, which keeps Graph client secrets and broader Graph behavior behind a production-shaped API boundary.

target.title: feat(clickclack): publish durable agent activity rows (commentary + tool)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/clickclack` channel extension only delivered the final prose reply, so a ClickClack channel showed nothing while an agent turn ran, even though the ClickClack server natively stores and renders durable `agent_commentary` / `agent_tool` message rows (with `turn_id` grouping and a dedicated non-inherited `agent_activity:write` bot scope). This PR adds an opt-in activity publisher to the extension: when an account sets `agentActivity: true` and its bot token carries `agent_activity:write`, streamed commentary and tool progress from the in-process `replyOptions.onItemEvent` seam are POSTed as durable activity rows (and PATCHed as snapshots grow), coalesced so one logical step becomes one row. Tool rows render through the shared `buildChannelProgressDraftLine` formatter, so ClickClack shows the same tool name + command detail as the Discord/Slack/Telegram progress lines. Publishing is best-effort: transport failures are logged and never interrupt final text delivery, and the flag defaults to off so stock setups and older ClickClack servers are untouched.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior:** With a ClickClack account bound to an agent, sending a channel message runs the agent turn invisibly: no commentary, no tool activity, only the final reply. After this PR (with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token carrying `agent_activity:write`), durable commentary and tool rows stream into the channel while the turn runs.

**Real environment:** Real gateway built from this repo (`pnpm build`, `node openclaw.mjs gateway`), real ClickClack server built from upstream `clickclack` source at `main@51a375d` (`go build ./apps/api/cmd/clickclack`, sqlite, dev bootstrap), real model turns (`anthropic/claude-opus-4-6`) with exec tools, stock ClickClack web UI in Chromium driven through the composer. BEFORE gateway is built at the merge base `bd2740fedc`; AFTER gateway is built at this PR head. Same server instance, same channel name, same steps.

**Exact steps:**
1. Run the ClickClack server (`clickclack serve`, dev bootstrap) and create an empty `#agent-demo` channel.
2. Configure `channels.clickclack` with `baseUrl`, a bot token, `replyMode: "agent"`; BEFORE uses the merge-base build (no `agentActivity` key exists there), AFTER uses this PR's build with `agentActivity: true` and a bot token that carries `agent_activity:write`.
3. Start the gateway, open `#agent-demo` in the ClickClack web UI, and type into the composer: "Check what OS version this server is running, how much free disk space it has, and how many files are in your workspace directory. Narrate what you are doing between steps, then give me a two-line summary."
4. Watch the channel while the turn runs, then open the reply thread.

**Evidence (before):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-before-prose-only.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/before-final_sheet.png)

**Evidence (after):** https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/clickclack-after-agent-activity.gif (frame-by-frame contact sheet: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ragesaq/openclaw/proof/clickclack-agent-activity-evidence/after-final_sheet.png)

**Observed result:** BEFORE: the channel stays empty for the whole turn; a lone "1 reply" thread chip appears at the end and the thread contains only the final summary. AFTER: one `agent_commentary` row ("Checking OS version, disk space, and workspace file count all at once…") and three `agent_tool` rows ("🛠️ show /etc/os-release …", "🛠️ df -h /", "🛠️ find files in … -> run wc") stream into the channel during the turn, grouped by `turn_id`, and the final summary lands in the thread as before. Stored rows verified over the ClickClack REST API (`kind: agent_commentary` / `agent_tool`, shared `turn_id`).

**What was not tested:** DM conversations (the publisher targets `direct_conversation_id`, covered by unit tests, but the live capture is a channel); multi-account setups beyond one account; a ClickClack server predating the activity kinds (degradation there relies on the opt-in default staying off plus best-effort error logging, exercised in unit tests, not live); non-embedded (CLI-backend) agent runtimes.

### Clean-room validation
- Command: fresh clone of `pull/99954/head` (`82bc62ed46`) inside a stock `node:22-bookworm` container: `git fetch --depth 1 origin pull/99954/head && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack`
- Provider / lease: plain Docker container (crabbox delegated providers unavailable on this host: `blacksmith` and `sbx` binaries not installed, no AWS credentials — stated per proof policy rather than skipped silently)
- Result: **34/34 tests passed, 6/6 files** on the fresh clone

### Tests, build, lint
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/clickclack` — 6 files, 32 tests passed (includes 7 new activity-publisher tests + new accounts/http-client/inbound cases)
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — exit 0
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — exit 0
- `pnpm oxlint extensions/clickclack` — 0 warnings, 0 errors
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — bundled channel-config metadata in sync (regenerated in this PR for the new `agentActivity` key)
- `pnpm build` — full build passes; the AFTER evidence runs this exact build

## Findings
None open. Two defects were caught and fixed during my own validation pass before posting: (1) the generated bundled channel-config metadata initially wasn't regenerated, which made gateway startup reject `agentActivity` as an unknown key; (2) item events are gated on tool-summary visibility, so the publisher declares channel-owned progress rendering (`suppressDefaultToolProgressMessages: true`) to receive events regardless of session verbose mode, matching the draft-compositor precedent.

## Lineage
None. Consumes the existing `replyOptions.onItemEvent` / `commentaryProgressEnabled` seam already used by the Discord/Telegram/Slack draft paths. The ClickClack server side (activity kinds, `turn_id`, `agent_activity:write` scope) is already merged upstream in the ClickClack repo.

## Remaining risk
Low. The feature is off by default and fully additive; with the flag off the extension behavior is byte-identical to before. With the flag on, publisher failures are logged best-effort and cannot break final delivery (single promise chain isolates transport errors). The main thing to watch is row volume on long multi-tool turns: one row per tool call plus one per commentary segment, PATCH-coalesced within a 700ms debounce window.

## Summary

- Preserves local package overrides during package update flows, including standalone added `dist` files, and reports the recovery bundle when overrides are not reapplied.
- Keeps content-inventory validation strict for new tarballs while allowing already-published `2026.6.5` / `2026.6.5-beta.6` packages that predate `dist/postinstall-content-inventory.json`.
- Repairs the `main` merge conflict on `src/cli/update-cli.ts` and `src/infra/update-runner.ts`, then refreshes the branch to current `upstream/main`.
- Adds the missing zh-CN glossary entries needed for the docs check after the latest main merge.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `pnpm docs:list`

## Summary - add policy evidence for `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` and `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` entries - add `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` policy metadata and shape validation - report `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` when policy-denied node commands are not denied by OpenClaw config - document the new policy rule in the Policy CLI and plugin reference docs - classify `gateway.nodes.allowCommands.*` in policy config coverage  ## Policy syntax / evidence / finding contract  Policy syntax added by this PR:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` is an exact, case-sensitive deny-superset rule. An equal-or-stricter policy must include every command required by the baseline deny list. Empty or missing `denyCommands` means this rule is not active.  OpenClaw config evidence collected by policy doctor:  ```jsonc {   "gateway": {     "nodes": {       "allowCommands": ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"],       "denyCommands": ["system.run"]     }   } } ```  The evidence scanner records concrete config entries as:  ```text kind=nodeAllowCommand command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/allowCommands/#2 kind=nodeDenyCommand  command=system.run source=oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands/#0 ```  Finding emitted when policy requires a deny but config does not provide it:  ```json {   "checkId": "policy/gateway-node-command-denied",   "severity": "error",   "message": "Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config.",   "path": "openclaw config",   "ocPath": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "target": "oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "requirement": "oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands",   "fixHint": "Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review." } ```  The finding clears when the config deny list contains the required exact command id. `allowCommands` evidence is collected for coverage and context; this PR only enforces the policy deny-superset contract.  ## Real behavior proof  Behavior or issue addressed: Managed policy can now require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be denied in OpenClaw config via `gateway.nodes.denyCommands`. The policy doctor reports the missing config deny and clears once the config denylist covers the policy denylist.  Real environment tested: Windows 11 PowerShell, `C:\src\openclaw-fork` checkout at PR head `cfe901e17963d9fe1833266a2758f125d7a51762`, source-harness invocation of the real policy doctor health checks through `runDoctorLintChecks`. The harness wrote real temporary `openclaw.jsonc` and `policy.jsonc` files under `%TEMP%`; no cloud gateway or Lobster deployment was involved.  Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Ran a Node/tsx source harness from the repo root that imported `registerPolicyDoctorChecks` and `runDoctorLintChecks`. 2. Case `missing-config-deny`: wrote `policy.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]` and `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.allowCommands: ["mcp.help", "mcp.invoke", "system.run"]` and no config `denyCommands`. 3. Case `satisfied-config-deny`: wrote the same policy plus `openclaw.jsonc` with `gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"]`.  Evidence after fix: ```text CASE missing-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-missing-config-deny-Xk9xXX openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] finding.checkId: policy/gateway-node-command-denied finding.severity: error finding.message: Gateway node command 'system.run' is denied by policy but not denied by OpenClaw config. finding.ocPath: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.target: oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.requirement: oc://policy.jsonc/gateway/nodes/denyCommands finding.fixHint: Add 'system.run' to gateway.nodes.denyCommands or update policy after review.  CASE satisfied-config-deny workspace: C:\Users\giodl\AppData\Local\Temp\oc-policy-satisfied-config-deny-jngRgn openclaw.jsonc gateway.nodes: {"allowCommands":["mcp.help","mcp.invoke","system.run"],"denyCommands":["system.run"]} policy.jsonc gateway.nodes.denyCommands: ["system.run"] policy/gateway-node-command-denied findings: none ```  Observed result after fix: The missing config-deny case emits exactly one `policy/gateway-node-command-denied` error targeted at `oc://openclaw.config/gateway/nodes/denyCommands`. The satisfied config-deny case emits no finding for that check.  What was not tested: This was source-harness policy doctor proof, not a live Lobster/cloud gateway run. Cloud gateway rollout behavior for `system.run` allowlisting remains a separate Lobster deployment concern.  ## Validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts --reporter=dot` - `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json` - `./node_modules/oxfmt/bin/oxfmt --check extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts scripts/lib/policy-config-coverage.jsonc` - `./node_modules/oxlint/bin/oxlint extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts` - `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt.cmd --check docs/cli/policy.md docs/plugins/reference/policy.md extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/scopes/gateway.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts extensions/policy/src/policy-state.ts scripts/lib/policy-config-coverage.jsonc` - `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md` - `git diff --check` - `pnpm tsgo:test:extensions` - `codex review --base upstream/main`  ## Notes This gives managed policy a way to require privileged gateway node commands such as `system.run` to be present in `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` unless a deployment intentionally relaxes policy. The rule uses the existing `denylist-superset` strictness pattern and keeps node command IDs case-sensitive.## Real behavior proofBehavior or issue addressed:Gateway node command policy coverage stays intact after restacking onto current `upstream/main`; the stack also resolves the `plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` merge conflict by preserving CI budget-env isolation.Real environment tested:Windows PowerShell in `C:\src\openclaw-fork` on the restacked policy series, top head `7aebf26a24` with the foundation branch head `8b97698d63`. This is a source-harness proof; it does not start a packaged OpenClaw binary or make live LLM calls.Exact steps or command run after this patch:1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/policy/src/doctor/metadata.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/register.test.ts extensions/policy/src/doctor/strictness.test.ts src/flows/doctor-repair-flow.test.ts --reporter=dot`2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts --reporter=dot`3. `pnpm tsgo:extensions`4. `pnpm lint:extensions`5. `git diff --check`
6. `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json`Evidence after fix:The focused policy/core/CLI/tooling Vitest run passed 10 core repair-flow tests, 7 SDK surface tooling tests, 13 policy CLI tests, and 334 policy doctor/doctor-lint tests. `tsgo:extensions`, `lint:extensions`, `git diff --check`, and `node --import tsx scripts/check-policy-config-coverage.ts --check --json` all exited 0.Observed result after fix:Gateway node command policy coverage remains green, and the restacked branch no longer has the generated SDK surface test conflict against current `main`.What was not tested:No packaged CLI smoke, live provider run, or live LLM call was run for this restack proof.

target.title: fix: roll rounded durations into seconds
target.body:
Closes #99978

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading duration output could see `1000ms` when a sub-second value such as 999.6ms rounded up to the next unit boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The duration helpers now decide whether to stay in milliseconds after calculating the rounded millisecond value, so values that round to 1000ms flow through the existing seconds formatting path. This keeps the fix limited to the shared formatter behavior and adds regression coverage for all three affected duration displays.

## User Impact

Timing text now stays in the expected unit scheme: rounded sub-second durations display as `1s` instead of the confusing `1000ms` edge case.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: `formatDurationPrecise`, `formatDurationCompact`, and `formatDurationHuman` return `1s` for 999.6ms.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `git diff --check` passed.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts --reporter=verbose` passed: 1 file, 60 tests.
  - `node --import tsx -e "const m=await import('./src/infra/format-time/format-duration.ts'); console.log(JSON.stringify({precise:m.formatDurationPrecise(999.6),compact:m.formatDurationCompact(999.6),human:m.formatDurationHuman(999.6)}))"` printed `{"precise":"1s","compact":"1s","human":"1s"}`.
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result: all affected duration helpers roll rounded 1000ms values into the existing seconds display path.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - No broad suite or full typecheck run; this is a two-file formatter fix and the focused formatter test covers the changed behavior.
  - First focused test attempt failed because the fresh isolated worktree had no `node_modules` (`OPENCLAW_MISSING_VITEST`); `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` completed successfully and the same focused test passed afterward.

AI-assisted with Codex.

target.title: refactor(security): consolidate secret primitives
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Secret display masking and constant-time secret comparison were split across a generic utility, plugin-local wrappers, and ad hoc forwarding helpers. That duplicated security-sensitive contracts and made exact behavior harder to audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Move the existing API-key display policy from `src/utils` to the security owner boundary without changing its empty, short-value, control-character, prefix/suffix, or UTF-16 code-unit behavior.
- Keep constant-time string comparison as exact padded UTF-8 byte equality, including equal-length `timingSafeEqual` inputs and explicit original-length rejection.
- Remove Browser, Voice Call, Webhooks, and Zalo forwarding wrappers so callers use the existing canonical Plugin SDK comparison export directly.
- Keep Talk Voice's one-consumer prefix display helper local instead of adding a new public Plugin SDK subpath.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. Existing masked output remains byte-for-byte stable for covered inputs, and authentication/webhook comparisons retain exact string equality without unequal-length short-circuiting.

## Evidence

- LOC after trim: 15 files, `+87/-88` overall; production `+18/-44` (net `-26`); tests `+69/-44` (net `+25`); docs/generated/SDK contract `0`.
- Focused tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/secret-mask.test.ts src/security/secret-equal.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server.auth-token-gates-http.test.ts extensions/voice-call/src/webhook-security.test.ts extensions/webhooks/src/http.test.ts extensions/zalo/src/monitor.webhook.test.ts` (5 shards, 74 tests).
- SDK exports: `node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs`.
- Exact-head build: delegated Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwqbd0qcy7kdbm0drem3b76t`, Actions run `28717952266`, `pnpm build` passed.
- Exact-head changed gate: delegated Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kwqcenwwqjx66v5wqxessepp`, Actions run `28718419048`, full `pnpm check:changed` passed.
- Autoreview: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --prompt-file /tmp/secret-primitives-review.txt --stream-engine-output` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings, confidence `0.97`.
- Head SHA: `ea26400bb0d777c9ab7b615253675682535e5c53`.

Known proof note: current `origin/main`'s committed Plugin SDK API baseline hash is stale relative to a clean regeneration; this PR has no Plugin SDK surface diff, and the subpath export check plus build are green.

Small private type aliases that only rename an existing type add vocabulary without adding narrowing, branding, ownership, or compatibility value. They make signatures harder to trace and obscure the canonical type.

Audit exact identity aliases and remove 20 non-exported, one-use aliases across core and bundled plugins. Each use now names the existing canonical type directly. ## What Problem This Solves

Wave 3 of the shared utility consolidation found that canonical OpenClaw home-path behavior was split between `src/infra/home-dir.ts` and generic `src/utils.ts`. Resolution already had a focused owner, while `resolveUserPath` was duplicated and user-facing home presentation remained embedded in the broad utility module.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Makes `src/infra/home-dir.ts` the single owner for effective/OS home resolution and user-path expansion.
- Moves display-only home shortening into focused internal `src/infra/home-dir-display.ts`.
- Keeps `src/utils.ts` as the existing compatibility facade, preserving export identity and callers.
- Keeps terminal token-safe display, daemon/service policy, sandbox containment, config/state ownership, URL/media paths, shell expansion, and package/plugin-local contracts separate.
- Avoids expanding `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime`; the display module is not part of an SDK barrel.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. HOME/USERPROFILE/homedir precedence, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `~`/`~/`/`~\\`, unsupported `~user`, blank/relative/absolute paths, separators, normalization, fallback behavior, and display prefixes remain unchanged.

target.title: feat(tencent): add Tencent Hy3 provider (TokenHub and TokenPlan)
target.body:
Closes #99069

## Maintainer Note

TokenPlan support is intentionally included in this PR. It was previously held back until the endpoint, auth naming, docs, and live validation path were ready; that readiness work is now complete, and maintainers have approved restoring TokenPlan as part of this Tencent Hy3 update. ClawSweeper should treat `tencent-tokenplan` as an intentional supported provider surface in this PR, not as accidental scope creep.

## What Problem This Solves

Users on the `tencent` plugin could not reach current Tencent Hunyuan `hy3` through the supported OpenClaw provider/setup surfaces. The old plugin only exposed TokenHub `hy3-preview`, so onboarding, auth env detection, provider catalog discovery, docs, and config validation did not provide a complete path for `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit Tencent Hy3 support for both official endpoint families:

- Provider ids: `tencent-tokenhub`, `tencent-tokenplan`
- Model catalog:
  - `tencent-tokenhub`: `hy3-preview`, `hy3`
  - `tencent-tokenplan`: `hy3`
- Auth env vars: `TOKENHUB_API_KEY`, `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`
- Onboarding choices: `tokenhub-api-key`, `tokenplan-api-key`
- Direct onboarding flags: `--tokenhub-api-key`, `--tokenplan-api-key`

TokenPlan intentionally uses the same short env-var naming convention as TokenHub: `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`, not `TENCENT_TOKENPLAN_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

- Users can select `hy3` on TokenHub or TokenPlan through normal model refs and onboarding.
- TokenPlan works through `TOKENPLAN_API_KEY` without manual provider config.
- Overlay-only provider config such as `models.providers.tencent-tokenplan.timeoutSeconds` validates like other built-in provider overlays.
- `hy3-preview` remains available on TokenHub.

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## Summary

Replace unbounded `response.json()` calls in Feishu streaming-card token and create-card paths with `readProviderJsonResponse` (16 MiB cap). Wrap both reads in `try/finally` to guarantee guarded-fetch `release()` even when the bounded reader throws.

Closes #98837 (previous submission, closed for missing proof).

## What Problem This Solves

Feishu streaming card API responses are read via unbounded `response.json()`. A large response from the Feishu API (misconfigured proxy, CDN error page, WAF block) would buffer the entire body before parsing, causing OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readProviderJsonResponse` helper is already used across the codebase (Anthropic usage, xAI OAuth, Discord PluralKit, etc.) for the same reason. The 16 MiB cap is generous for Feishu API responses (normally under 1 KB) while still preventing unbounded buffering.

## User Impact

Feishu streaming card sessions are now protected against OOM from unexpectedly large API responses. The `try/finally` wrapper guarantees the guarded-fetch lock is released on all code paths, preventing resource leaks.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof** — terminal output from `proof-feishu-streaming-card.mts`:

```
=== Proof: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads ===

Max read cap: 16777216 bytes (16 MiB)
Body size:    18874368 bytes (18 MiB)

Chunks enqueued: 18
Stream cancelled: true
Elapsed: 45ms
Error: feishu.streamingCard.token: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes
Read stopped at cap: true

Result: PASS
readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized body, stream was cancelled before full 18 MiB buffered.

=== Before-fix comparison ===
Old: await response.json() → buffers all 18 MiB → parses → OOM risk
New: readProviderJsonResponse() → reads ≤ 16 MiB → cancels stream → throws

PASS: feishu streaming-card bounded JSON reads prevent OOM.
```

**Tests** (20 passed):

```
pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

Includes 2 new oversized response rejection tests that verify:
- Token responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, `release()` called
- Create-card responses > 16 MiB are rejected, stream cancelled, both `release()` calls made

**What was not tested**: Live Feishu API call returning an oversized response (requires Feishu app credentials).

## Risk

Low. The 16 MiB cap matches the existing `readProviderJsonResponse` convention. Feishu API responses are normally under 1 KB. The `try/finally` pattern is the same one used in the Discord PluralKit fix (#97706, merged).

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts
  - 24 passed.
- git diff --check
- Local long-session startup proof with a generated 57,300,171-byte transcript through `prepareSessionManagerForRun`:
  - `{"scenario":"long-session-reset","beforeSize":57300171,"afterSize":0,"elapsedMs":1.22}`
  - `{"scenario":"capped-blank-prefix-corrupt-header","rejected":true,"preserved":true,"elapsedMs":12.07}`

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{

  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",

      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved.
